Plot the exceedance probabilities of the site effects

Source: R/plot-exceedance.R
plot_exceedance.Rd

For each site, plot_exceedance() shows the exceedance probability, i.e., the posterior probability that the effect is above (or below) a threshold, as computed by exceedance_prob(). If cutoff is specified, a line marks that probability and the caption gives the number of sites that reach it.

Usage

plot_exceedance(
  x,
  threshold = 0,
  direction = c("above", "below"),
  sort = TRUE,
  cutoff = NULL,
  max_sites = 100,
  scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

threshold

Threshold for the effects, a number in the units of the estimates.

direction

One of "above" (the default) for the probability that the effect is greater than threshold, or "below" for the probability that it is not.

sort

If TRUE (the default), the sites are ordered by their probabilities. If FALSE, they are in the order of the data.

cutoff

An optional probability between 0 and 1, which is marked by a dashed line.

max_sites

Maximum number of sites that are plotted with labels. See Details for how a larger number of sites is shown.

scale

Positive number by which threshold is multiplied in the axis label. See Details.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Up to max_sites sites are shown as labeled points. If there are more, the probabilities are shown as a curve in increasing order or, when sort = FALSE, as points in the order of the data.

threshold is specified in the units of the estimates, as in exceedance_prob(). scale only changes the units in which the threshold appears in the axis label: with threshold = 0.02 and scale = 100, the label reads "above 2".

The number of sites at or above cutoff is based on the posterior probability of each site separately. It is not the result of a procedure that controls an error rate over many sites, as the caption also notes.

See also

exceedance_prob(), plot_sites(), vignette("plots")

Examples

# The probability that the callback gap of a firm is positive, and the
# firms for which it is at least 0.95.
plot_exceedance(krw_fit, cutoff = 0.95)


# The probability that the gap exceeds 2 percentage points.
plot_exceedance(krw_fit, threshold = 0.02, scale = 100)


# 1,500 sites: a curve.
plot_exceedance(twin_towers_fit, cutoff = 0.9)
#> There are 1500 sites to draw, more than `max_sites` (100), so they are drawn without labels. Raise `max_sites` to label them.
